messages.content: I'm planning a series of long weekend getaways for the upcoming year and I need to know when they'll occur in my country. Could you fetch me the list of long weekends for Canada in the year 2023? I'd like to integrate this information into my holiday planning app.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the **long‑weekend** holidays that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a statutory holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday, giving you a three‑day break (Friday‑Saturday‑Sunday or Saturday‑Sunday‑Monday).  

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Family Day** (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, etc.) | Feb 20 | Friday | Feb 20–22 |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 | Friday | Apr 7–9 |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 | Monday | May 20–22 |
| **Canada Day** (observed) | Jul 3 | Monday (observed) | Jul 1–3 |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 | Monday | Sep 2–4 |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 | Monday | Oct 7–9 |
| **Remembrance Day** | Nov 11 | Friday | Nov 11–13 |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 | Monday | Dec 23–25 |

> **Notes**  
> * **New Year’s Day** fell on Sunday (Jan 1) and was observed on Monday (Jan 2), but it didn’t create a three‑day weekend.  
> * **Boxing Day** (Dec 26) was observed on Dec 27 (Wednesday), so it didn’t form a long weekend.  
> * Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, St. George’s Day in Prince Edward Island, etc.) that may also produce long weekends, but the table above lists the nationwide statutory holidays that most Canadians would have used for planning.

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app! If you need province‑specific long weekends or a different definition of “long weekend,” just let me know.
